theory.heading: Combine selected theme ideas
theory.body: Begin by choosing useful ideas from your personal-theme research. A concept may combine initials with a hobby symbol, a place outline with an animal shape, or another meaningful pairing. The aim is not to fit every theme into one design. Select features that work together and communicate a clear personal meaning. Each combination should have a recognisable main idea rather than becoming a collection of unrelated details. When choosing features, consider what should attract attention first and which shapes can support the message without making the emblem confusing.

theory.heading: Create three distinct thumbnails
theory.body: Develop three quick thumbnail drawings that explore genuinely different concepts. Thumbnails are small, fast sketches used to test arrangements before spending time on detail. Change the main symbol, shape combination, visual balance or placement between concepts. Three slight redraws of the same arrangement do not provide strong design evidence. For example, changing only the size of one symbol would not create a clearly different concept. Each thumbnail should show another possible direction and remain simple enough for the overall idea to be understood quickly.

theory.heading: Annotate arrangement and meaning
theory.body: Add brief annotations beside each thumbnail to explain the selected theme, the arrangement of shapes and the intended meaning. An annotation might identify the main symbol, explain why two features were combined or describe what should be noticed first. Clear notes help another person understand decisions that may not be obvious from the sketch alone. Review the three concepts side by side and check that each offers a distinct response. If a concept or annotation is unclear, revise it or ask before continuing. Current school SOPs and teacher directions control all actual workshop activity.

questions.question: What should guide the selection of ideas for an emblem concept?
choices: A clear personal meaning
The largest number of symbols
Another student's finished design
The most detailed reference image
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Selected features should work together to communicate a clear personal meaning.
questions.retryFeedback: Review Combine selected theme ideas and focus on what the chosen features should communicate.

questions.question: Why should a concept avoid too many unrelated details?
choices: They make every symbol identical
They can make the emblem confusing
They prevent the use of annotations
They always create an empty layout
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Unrelated details can weaken the main idea and make the emblem difficult to understand.
questions.retryFeedback: Return to Combine selected theme ideas and identify why features must work together.

questions.question: What should a student consider when arranging selected features?
choices: Which online design is most popular
How to copy every research image
What should attract attention first
How to include every possible theme
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Considering visual priority helps create a clear arrangement with a recognisable main idea.
questions.retryFeedback: Re-read Combine selected theme ideas and focus on the question about visual attention.

questions.question: What is a thumbnail drawing?
choices: A finished detailed emblem
A copied reference image
A written explanation only
A small quick sketch used to test an idea
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. A thumbnail is a quick, small sketch used to explore arrangements before adding detail.
questions.retryFeedback: Review Create three distinct thumbnails and locate the definition of a thumbnail.

questions.question: What makes three emblem concepts genuinely distinct?
choices: They use the same design with tiny size changes
They explore different main ideas or arrangements
They contain identical shapes in identical positions
They are traced from three finished emblems
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Distinct concepts explore meaningfully different symbols, combinations or arrangements.
questions.retryFeedback: Return to Create three distinct thumbnails and identify what should change between concepts.

questions.question: Which set provides weak evidence of three concepts?
choices: Three different theme combinations
Three different main symbols
Three minor redraws of one arrangement
Three clearly different layouts
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Minor redraws do not demonstrate the exploration of separate design directions.
questions.retryFeedback: Re-read Create three distinct thumbnails and focus on what does not count as distinct concepts.

questions.question: Why should thumbnails remain simple?
choices: So annotations are unnecessary
So every concept looks the same
So personal meaning can be removed
So the overall idea can be understood quickly
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Simple thumbnails allow the main concept and arrangement to be judged quickly.
questions.retryFeedback: Review the final sentence of Create three distinct thumbnails and identify the benefit of simplicity.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an annotation beside a thumbnail?
choices: To explain the arrangement and intended meaning
To add unrelated decoration
To provide a construction sequence
To replace the drawing
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Annotations explain design decisions that may not be obvious from the sketch alone.
questions.retryFeedback: Return to Annotate arrangement and meaning and focus on what the notes should communicate.

questions.question: Which annotation gives useful design evidence?
choices: I drew this quickly
This design is good
The larger initial is the main feature, and the wave shape represents my local river
The emblem uses some shapes
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. This annotation identifies the arrangement, visual priority and personal meaning.
questions.retryFeedback: Re-read Annotate arrangement and meaning and identify the types of decisions a useful note explains.

questions.question: What should a student check when comparing the three concepts?
choices: Whether all three are nearly identical
Whether every concept contains all three themes
Whether each copies a finished emblem
Whether each provides a distinct design response
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Each concept should offer a clearly different possible direction for the emblem.
questions.retryFeedback: Review Annotate arrangement and meaning and focus on the side-by-side comparison check.

written.prompt: Describe three distinct emblem concepts developed from selected personal themes. Explain the main symbol, arrangement and intended meaning of each concept.
written.sentenceStarter: Concept one combines ___ and ___ by ___. Concept two is different because ___. Concept three explores ___.
written.example: Concept one combines my initials with a fish profile, with the initials as the main feature. Concept two places a river line inside a simple circle. Concept three combines a mountain outline with a significant number, creating a clearly different arrangement and meaning.
